Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-001, AERA-DA-002, AERA-DA-003, AERA-DA-006, AERA-AUTH-101, AERA-AUTH-107, AERA-DA-033
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Validate grant integrity, issuer authority, scope, and chain to an approved trust anchor; separate grant, authorization, and enforcement roles. D: Detect invalid issuer, anchor, integrity, scope, or authorization-state changes. C: Reject or quarantine the forged grant and invalidate dependent authorization. R: Re-establish authority from a known-good root and reconcile any initiated effect.
Representative negative test: Submit a well-formed, correctly signed grant whose signer is authenticated but lacks authority to grant the requested decision class; attempt the effect through both the normal DAF path and the effect interface. Expected result: no permit and no effect.
Expected evidence: Approved trust-anchor and accountable-authority inventory; delegation schema; chain-validation trace; role-separation matrix; negative grant cases; enforcement denial receipt; revocation or quarantine record; effect-observation record showing no unauthorized effect.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-002, AERA-DA-003, AERA-DA-005, AERA-AUTH-105, AERA-AUTH-107, AERA-AUTH-108, AERA-DA-031
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Require immutable parent references, complete-chain validation, attenuation, and deny precedence. D: Identify missing, reordered, substituted, ambiguous, or unauthorized parents during validation and reconstruction. C: Reject the chain and invalidate descendants. R: Reissue or re-resolve the chain from approved records and reassess affected transactions.
Representative negative test: Remove an intermediate parent, reorder two parents, and substitute a valid grant rooted in the wrong authority domain. Expected result: all variants are rejected before authorization and are distinguishable in the audit record.
Expected evidence: Trust-anchor inventory; parent-reference and chain-validation logs; malformed-chain corpus and results; precedence tests; descendant invalidation evidence; causal reconstruction showing the exact fault.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-002, AERA-DA-003, AERA-DA-004, AERA-DA-007, AERA-DA-022, AERA-DA-028, AERA-DA-031
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Deny subdelegation by default; require derived-grant attenuation; bind downstream actor, tool, target, effect, and expiry; deny direct effect access. D: Preserve transitive actor, tool, and grant attribution. C: Reject the derived request, revoke or quarantine dependent credentials, and block the effect path. R: Restore operation using an explicitly approved attenuated grant.
Representative negative test: Give Actor A a non-subdelegable grant, then have A invoke Actor B or a broker service to perform the effect using A's tool access. Expected result: target-domain enforcement rejects the request and records both the initiator and attempted deputy.
Expected evidence: Parent and child grant comparison; subdelegation policy; workload identity and tool-credential records; transitive audit trace; denied effect receipt; credential revocation record; recovery transaction under a valid grant.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-002, AERA-DA-005, AERA-DA-017, AERA-DA-024, AERA-DA-026, AERA-DA-033, AERA-AUTH-106, AERA-ENF-103
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Bound grant and authorization lifetime, use, audience, and context; distribute revocation within a declared maximum. D: Monitor expiry, revocation, actor integrity, and context change at both DAF and enforcement points. C: Reject stale or replayed artifacts and invalidate descendants. R: Reauthorize from current authority after partition reconciliation and reconcile any partial effect.
Representative negative test: Authorize once, revoke the parent grant, isolate an enforcement cache until after the maximum propagation time, then replay the authorization. Expected result: rejection in connected and partitioned modes; no new effect.
Expected evidence: Revocation-latency measurement; cache and partition test results; token validity/use records; enforcement rejection receipt; descendant invalidation trace; post-partition reconciliation evidence.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-005, AERA-DA-007, AERA-DA-012, AERA-DA-024, AERA-DA-033, AERA-DA-034, AERA-ENF-103
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Bind workload identity to owner, role, model or software version, runtime integrity, tools, consequence ceiling, and exact proposal. D: Detect actor, binary, model, configuration, or runtime-integrity mismatch and post-release change. C: Reject or quarantine the substituted workload and revoke dependent authorization. R: Restore an approved version and initiate a new transaction.
Representative negative test: Obtain a permit for workload version N, then execute the same proposal from version N+1 or a different model using the same logical actor identifier. Expected result: enforcement rejects actor substitution and the prior permit is invalidated.
Expected evidence: Workload identity registry; version/configuration baseline; attestation or equivalent runtime-integrity evidence; actor-binding test; enforcement rejection receipt; monitoring alert; rollback and reauthorization trace.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-001, AERA-DA-008, AERA-DA-009, AERA-DA-026, AERA-DA-031, AERA-DA-034
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Use attributable, versioned, integrity-protected, machine-testable intent with explicit objectives, constraints, prohibitions, priority, and expiry. D: Compare effective intent version and conflict resolution against the transaction and observed effect. C: Invalidate authorization on material intent change; defer, deny, or escalate unresolved conflict. R: Restore an approved intent baseline and reauthorize.
Representative negative test: Issue a permit under intent version 7, then supersede a prohibited outcome or priority without accountable-owner approval while retaining the prior intent identifier. Expected result: integrity/version failure, permit invalidation, and no effect.
Expected evidence: Signed intent objects; intent change history; precedence and conflict tests; intent-to-effect trace; context-change alert; invalidation latency; rollback and new-transaction evidence.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-008, AERA-DA-009, AERA-DA-010, AERA-DA-026, AERA-DA-031, AERA-DA-034
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Approve and integrity-protect policy/configuration versions; bind exact policy inputs and evaluator version to each disposition; reject unapproved rollback. D: Detect version, signature, baseline, and evaluator mismatch. C: Quarantine the unapproved bundle and invalidate dispositions derived from it. R: Restore the approved baseline, reassess affected transactions, and verify rollback.
Representative negative test: Replace the current restrictive policy bundle with an authentic but obsolete permissive version and replay a previously valid evaluator image. Expected result: rollback rejection and no permit.
Expected evidence: Approved signed policy inventory; configuration baseline; disposition record with policy/evaluator versions; rollback and downgrade test results; alert and quarantine record; restoration and reassessment trace.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-001, AERA-DA-006, AERA-DA-009, AERA-DA-011, AERA-DA-018, AERA-DA-027, AERA-CONS-102, AERA-CONS-103, AERA-CONS-105
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Apply the worst credible direct, secondary, cumulative, propagated, and irreversible consequence; prevent proposer-only downgrade; preserve non-compensatory hard gates. D: Independently reclassify boundary cases and monitor aggregate exposure. C: Reject the downgrade and apply the higher control floor. R: Narrow the proposal materially or obtain an approved reassessment and new authorization.
Representative negative test: Present the same physical or digital effect as CC-1 after it was approved as CC-3 by splitting it into smaller requests and averaging severity with reversible attributes. Expected result: classification remains at the controlling class and high-consequence controls remain active.
Expected evidence: Approved classification rubric; accountable owner and role matrix; inter-rater and boundary-case results; cumulative-effect analysis; downgrade approval record if applicable; policy trace showing the controlling class.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-012, AERA-DA-017, AERA-DA-024, AERA-DA-026, AERA-ENF-102, AERA-ENF-103, AERA-ENF-105, AERA-IF-002
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Canonicalize and bind actor, action, target, parameters, tool, sequence, evidence manifest, context, and validity. D: Compare proposal digest and actual execution parameters at enforcement and receipt reconciliation. C: Reject mutation, replay, retargeting, or stale context. R: Preserve evidence, create a new transaction, and reconcile any partial effect.
Representative negative test: After authorization, change one consequential parameter or target while retaining the original token and transaction ID; repeat during a race between policy evaluation and dispatch. Expected result: both mutations are rejected before effect.
Expected evidence: Canonicalization specification; digest and version records; mutation, race, target-substitution, and replay test results; enforcement receipt; effect observation; reauthorization trace.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-013, AERA-DA-015, AERA-DA-016, AERA-DA-033, AERA-EVID-101, AERA-EVID-105, AERA-THR-001
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Authenticate evidence source and integrity; carry provenance, acquisition context, uncertainty, and limits; exclude or explicitly discount unverifiable evidence. D: Detect contradiction, impossible state, out-of-distribution input, and evidence-quality change. C: Quarantine or exclude the source and reevaluate dependent decisions. R: Acquire replacement evidence and reconcile effects authorized from suspect evidence.
Representative negative test: Inject a fabricated observation using a compromised but otherwise valid source credential, then provide a conflicting independent observation. Expected result: the system does not treat authentication as truth, exposes the contradiction, and follows the configured non-permit path.
Expected evidence: Source-identity and integrity records; evidence manifest; forged-source and contradiction test results; anomaly or plausibility alert; exclusion/quarantine policy trace; dependent-decision invalidation and reassessment evidence. AERA 1.1 RC1 gap-closure control retained in 1.2 WD: AERA-THR-001.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-012, AERA-DA-013, AERA-DA-015, AERA-DA-030, AERA-DA-031, AERA-IF-002, AERA-IF-004, AERA-IF-007
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Bind a transaction-specific evidence manifest; retain source and transformation lineage; supersede rather than erase corrections. D: Reconstruct raw-to-derived-to-decision links and detect a missing or altered lineage edge. C: Withdraw or quarantine the misbound artifact and invalidate reliance. R: Rebuild the evidence set from authoritative lineage and re-evaluate.
Representative negative test: Strip transformation metadata from a derived result and attach it to a different transaction with a compatible schema. Expected result: binding or lineage validation fails and no authorization relies on the artifact.
Expected evidence: Evidence manifest and schema; raw/derived relationship records; transaction binding; lineage reconstruction; rebinding and missing-link tests; correction/withdrawal record; reassessment trace.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-014, AERA-DA-018, AERA-DA-021, AERA-DA-029, AERA-EVID-104
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Define independence against the relevant sensor, data, model, provider, clock, network, power, operator, controller, and control-plane failure model. D: Detect shared dependencies and inject common-mode failures. C: Remove correlated sources from the independence count and defer, constrain, or deny when the floor is not met. R: Switch to a genuinely diverse source or approved degraded mode.
Representative negative test: Present two application feeds as independent although both inherit one GNSS receiver, clock distribution path, and provider control plane; fault the common source. Expected result: the quorum loses independence and nominal authority is not preserved.
Expected evidence: Failure-domain model; dependency graph; provenance and independence metadata; common-mode fault-injection results; quorum policy trace; degraded-mode and alternate-source evidence.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-016, AERA-DA-018, AERA-DA-019, AERA-DA-023, AERA-DA-033
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Preserve separately evaluated assurance claims, mandatory gates, calibration context, error measures, and known limits; prohibit scalar masking. D: Monitor calibration drift, out-of-distribution state, threshold changes, and dimension failures. C: Defer, constrain, deny, simulate, or quarantine when a mandatory claim fails. R: Restore an approved threshold/model version, recalibrate, and reassess.
Representative negative test: Inflate a scalar confidence score so it exceeds the permit threshold while authority validity or evidence adequacy is NOT-SATISFIED; separately alter calibration thresholds without approval. Expected result: no permit and a visible failed claim.
Expected evidence: Assurance-vector schema; policy decision table; calibration report and population; dimension-failure and threshold-tampering tests; drift alerts; rollback/recalibration record.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-017, AERA-DA-020, AERA-DA-021, AERA-DA-026, AERA-DA-033, AERA-PNT-001, AERA-PNT-002, AERA-PNT-003
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Bind source, time scale/reference frame, uncertainty, integrity, age, freshness, order, and validity thresholds to the decision contract. D: Detect source disagreement, spoofing/jamming indicators, timestamp rewriting, sequence violation, and holdover-limit exceedance. C: Invalidate affected authority/evidence and enter defined defer, deny, constraint, or degraded behavior. R: Transition to characterized alternate/holdover service, reconcile sequence, and reauthorize.
Representative negative test: Delay or rewrite one evidence timestamp so stale data appears fresh while a common reference is spoofed; continue beyond characterized holdover. Expected result: the source is not accepted or used nominally and the transaction cannot permit outside temporal limits.
Expected evidence: PNT evidence object; present/monitored/accepted/used instrumentation; source-selection and sequence logs; spoofing, delay, disagreement, and holdover tests; uncertainty characterization; degraded-mode and reauthorization trace.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-007, AERA-DA-012, AERA-DA-022, AERA-DA-024, AERA-DA-028, AERA-CY-001, AERA-CY-002, AERA-ENF-102, AERA-ENF-103
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Use workload identity and transaction-only, least-privileged, audience/target/action/time-scoped capabilities; independently mediate the effect. D: Compare actor, audience, action, target, parameters, and use state at enforcement. C: Reject, revoke, or quarantine the credential and actor. R: Reissue a properly scoped capability and reconcile attempted effects.
Representative negative test: Use a valid tool credential from the authorized actor against a different target, API audience, action, or time window, including direct invocation outside the transaction. Expected result: all out-of-scope attempts are denied.
Expected evidence: Workload identity and entitlement records; credential issuance and use logs; audience/target/action/time substitution tests; bypass test; enforcement denial receipt; revocation and reissuance trace.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-004, AERA-DA-007, AERA-DA-022, AERA-DA-024, AERA-DA-028, AERA-DA-031, AERA-ENF-102, AERA-ENF-103, AERA-THR-002
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Bind the requesting actor and authority context to the exact target-domain effect; deny ambient or bearer authority and effect-interface bypass. D: Preserve initiator, deputy, grant, and target-domain enforcement attribution. C: Reject the deputy's ambient-privilege action and revoke derived capabilities. R: Reissue an explicit attenuated target-domain grant and reconcile attempted effects.
Representative negative test: Have an authorized intermediary receive an unauthorized request and invoke the target using the intermediary's own standing credential without forwarding the original initiator/delegation. Expected result: target-domain enforcement rejects the request.
Expected evidence: Multi-hop identity/delegation trace; target-domain policy test; service credential scope; ambient-authority negative case; enforcement receipt; transitive audit reconstruction. AERA 1.1 RC1 gap-closure control retained in 1.2 WD: AERA-THR-002.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-011, AERA-DA-027, AERA-DA-033, AERA-CONS-104, AERA-CONS-106, AERA-THEORY-002
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Evaluate sequences, batches, concurrent actions, campaigns, and portfolios; reserve shared limits and prevent decomposition around a control floor. D: Monitor rolling exposure and interacting state across actors, tools, targets, and time. C: Stop or deny the sequence and revoke remaining reservations/authority. R: Reclassify the composed effect, compensate or restore state, and issue a new bounded transaction if acceptable.
Representative negative test: Have two actors submit individually permissible operations that together exceed a shared safety, financial, cyber, or physical limit; vary order and concurrency. Expected result: aggregate reservation prevents the prohibited state.
Expected evidence: Consequence and dependency model; shared-limit/reservation design; multi-actor sequence and concurrency tests; budget telemetry; denial/stop trace; recovery or compensation evidence.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-014, AERA-DA-027, AERA-DA-029, AERA-EVID-104
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Define quorum independence by controller, lineage, training data, evidence, operator, provider, clock, and failure domain rather than vote count. D: Detect shared control, provenance, synchronized anomalies, and correlated output. C: Discount captured members, fail the quorum, and defer/escalate. R: Convene an independently controlled review or evidence set and re-evaluate.
Representative negative test: Populate a three-agent quorum with agents that have separate identities but share one controller, model lineage, data source, and operator; coordinate a false vote. Expected result: the votes do not satisfy the independence requirement.
Expected evidence: Quorum policy; controller/model/data/operator provenance; failure-domain analysis; collusion and common-controller tests; disposition trace; independent-review reconstitution evidence.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-013, AERA-DA-015, AERA-DA-017, AERA-DA-030, AERA-DA-033, AERA-DA-034, AERA-DA-036
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Bind request, result, provider/service version, execution context, time, uncertainty, and validation method; require characterized fallback and independent effect enforcement. D: Verify provider identity, binding, freshness, plausibility, and service characterization. C: Exclude or quarantine the service/result and constrain or deny consequential use. R: Execute the characterized classical/local fallback, re-run validation, and reauthorize.
Representative negative test: Return a validly signed but stale or cross-request result from an external AI, optimizer, or quantum service, then make the provider unavailable. Expected result: misbound result rejection and controlled fallback without authority expansion.
Expected evidence: Service contract and provider identity; request/result binding records; version and uncertainty metadata; stale/misbound/plausibility tests; provider-failure exercise; fallback characterization; independent enforcement receipt.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-006, AERA-DA-009, AERA-DA-018, AERA-DA-022, AERA-DA-023, AERA-DA-025, AERA-DA-033, AERA-CY-002, AERA-IF-009, AERA-THR-003
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Require independently controlled effect mediation and explicit non-permit semantics; pre-engineer consequence-specific outage behavior. D: Detect bypass, timeout, overload, partition, and missing assurance state. C: Inhibit the effect path, quarantine the bypass route, and enter the declared degraded mode. R: Restore DAF service, reconcile queued/partial transactions, and reauthorize from current state.
Representative negative test: Saturate or partition the DAF, force a timeout, and attempt direct execution plus a default-allow response. Expected result: no silent permit, deterministic degraded behavior, and no unmediated effect.
Expected evidence: Trust-boundary and bypass analysis; capacity, overload, timeout, and partition tests; fail-safe/degraded-mode evidence; effect-interface denial receipt; continuity and reconciliation exercise. AERA 1.1 RC1 gap-closure control retained in 1.2 WD: AERA-THR-003.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-005, AERA-DA-010, AERA-DA-012, AERA-DA-017, AERA-DA-024, AERA-DA-025, AERA-DA-026, AERA-DA-033, AERA-ENF-102, AERA-ENF-105, AERA-IF-005, AERA-IF-010, AERA-THR-004
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Bind policy/context versions and transaction state; validate authorization, revocation, use, and proposal at enforcement; reject replay. D: Acknowledge execution state through integrity-protected receipts and reconcile version/use mismatches. C: Reject or revoke stale enforcement state and stop further effect. R: Synchronize current policy/context, reconcile partial execution, and create a new transaction.
Representative negative test: Delay policy/revocation replication to one enforcement point, then race duplicate or reordered requests across two points. Expected result: stale and duplicate attempts cannot create a second or unauthorized effect.
Expected evidence: Policy/context version records; replication-lag and race tests; authorization use counter; enforcement acknowledgements/receipts; replay rejection; mismatch alert; reconciliation trace. AERA 1.1 RC1 gap-closure control retained in 1.2 WD: AERA-THR-004.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-020, AERA-DA-031, AERA-DA-035, AERA-DA-036, AERA-DAF-116, AERA-ENF-105, AERA-ENF-107, AERA-IF-004, AERA-IF-007, AERA-THR-005
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Retain a tamper-evident, causally linked record with protected identity, integrity, ordering, and time quality; supersede rather than erase corrections. D: Perform completeness sampling, integrity verification, and end-to-end causal reconstruction. C: Isolate the corrupted logging path and preserve independent receipts/effect observations. R: Reconstruct from protected sources, document residual uncertainty, and reassess affected claims.
Representative negative test: Delete one disposition, reorder two state transitions, rewrite a timestamp, and forge an enforcement receipt while leaving local logs internally consistent. Expected result: integrity or completeness checks identify each break and reconstruction cannot falsely close the transaction.
Expected evidence: Cryptographic/log-integrity records; time-quality metadata; state-transition and enforcement receipts; deletion/reorder/retime/forgery tests; causal reconstruction; correction record; residual-risk disposition. AERA 1.1 RC1 gap-closure control retained in 1.2 WD: AERA-THR-005.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-006, AERA-DA-022, AERA-DA-023, AERA-DA-032, AERA-DA-033, AERA-EVID-106, AERA-ENF-104, AERA-HUM-104
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Separate recovery/override authority from the actor; define triggers, safe states, stop/contain/rollback/compensation actions, resources, and maximum recovery time. D: Monitor recovery readiness and exercise trigger-to-action paths. C: Invoke independently controlled stop, containment, quarantine, or takeover. R: Reach and verify the defined safe/recovered state and reconcile remaining exposure.
Representative negative test: Compromise the actor and primary control plane, then have the actor refuse stop, revoke, rollback, and quarantine commands. Expected result: an independent recovery path arrests the effect within the validated envelope.
Expected evidence: Recovery envelope and authority assignment; recovery-path independence analysis; protected override records; compromised-actor and control-plane exercise; time-to-safe-state measurement; effect verification and residual-exposure record.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-008, AERA-DA-010, AERA-DA-013, AERA-DA-019, AERA-DA-026, AERA-DA-031, AERA-DA-033, AERA-DA-034, AERA-MAT-008
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Treat model, prompt, policy, memory, data, tool, dependency, and threshold changes as versioned, provenance-bound, tested, approved, observable, and reversible configuration. D: Monitor drift, calibration, provenance, integrity, behavior, and material-change triggers after release. C: Inhibit promotion or operation, quarantine the changed artifact, and reduce authority. R: Roll back to the approved baseline, verify behavior, and reassess affected evidence and maturity claims.
Representative negative test: Poison feedback or memory to introduce a prohibited behavior without changing the nominal model identifier; separately alter a threshold through an unapproved online-learning path. Expected result: change is detected, authority does not expand, and rollback succeeds.
Expected evidence: Configuration and data provenance baseline; predeclared acceptance tests; approval and staged-release record; drift/calibration/integrity alerts; unauthorized-change test; rollback evidence; material-change reassessment.

Primary AERA requirements: AERA-DA-001, AERA-DA-006, AERA-DA-011, AERA-DA-016, AERA-DA-023, AERA-DA-029, AERA-DA-032, AERA-DA-035, AERA-HUM-102, AERA-HUM-103, AERA-THR-006
Prevention / detection / containment / r: P: Apply consequence-aware human-control modes, separation of duties, decisive review information, and independent review where required. D: Measure queue depth, review latency, override/approval patterns, explanation quality, workload, and error under stress. C: Throttle, defer, narrow, or deny requests; reassign review; require second-person concurrence for the defined threshold. R: Reconstruct affected approvals, reassess potentially perfunctory decisions, and restore sustainable oversight capacity.
Representative negative test: Flood reviewers with mixed low- and high-consequence requests, compressed deadlines, repetitive alerts, and misleading but plausible explanations; test whether approval accuracy or independence collapses or timeout becomes permission.
Expected evidence: Human-factors test plan; consequence-prioritized queue and throttle evidence; workload/latency/error telemetry; explanation-quality criteria; approval and second-person-review records; adverse-result analysis; reassessment and recovery record. AERA 1.1 RC1 gap-closure control retained in 1.2 WD: AERA-THR-006.
